scope: The linked Hôtel de Ville and medieval belfry at Place Godefroy de Bouillon. Includes the ten-bay brick and limestone front, balconied entrance, rear municipal wings, and attached square stone tower with its 1712-era octagonal upper stage.
geometryBasis: The city hall uses named multipolygon 7379169. The attached square tower is placed near its heritage point and its documented joint. The map inner ring is recorded as a map reference; source evidence establishes a square lower belfry with an octagonal upper stage.
sectionBasis: Three levels of brick and limestone, dark slate roof and additional attic, ten civic bays and two columns supporting the balcony. Retained belfry reaches 35 metres above the square.
limitations: The principal mapped city hall outline and belfry heritage location guide the model. The square belfry base and exact roof intersections are reconstructed from the archive view and architectural records.
Secondary façade bays and roof volumes are estimates. The historical museum photo informs retained belfry fabric and proportions. The municipal street front uses the 2004 public-domain exterior.
The original street terrain is preserved. Finished threshold and attached surfaces are approximate at terrain resolution.

sources.basis: Heritage inventory sets out the ten bays, three storeys and attic, limestone with brick, middle-storey segmental windows, square openings at the first and third levels, and the balcony supported by two columns.
The city measures the top of the attached belfry 35 m above Place Godefroy de Bouillon.
The tower retains paired pointed openings and four corner turrets. Its upper octagonal stage replaced the spire after the 1712 fire. The city hall was added on the southeast.
French national register identifies the attached protected belfry under the same place name.
